Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the guaranty association membership roster and every association registration; escalation to Head of Compliance, statutory-data questions to the Statutory Reporting Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska AS 21.80 (Alaska Insurance Guaranty Association Act, property/casualty) and AS 21.79 (Alaska Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association Act) re-read at each new admission; parallel member-insurer sections confirmed for Arizona (A.R.S. Title 20, Ch. 3), California (Ins. Code section 1063, CIGA) and Colorado (C.R.S. Title 10, Art. 4, Part 5) and carried across all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope processes.value: Certificate-of-authority maintenance feeding guaranty association membership upkeep: new state/line admissions, allocation to the correct assessment account (workers compensation, automobile, all-other for P&C; life, annuity, health for L&H), association contact registration, annual data-call response, and run-off membership on withdrawal — 51 jurisdictions, all writing companies

In-scope systems.value: The licence and certificate-of-authority register holds the state x line x writing-company matrix that drives the membership roster; association confirmation letters and data-call responses are filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Guaranty Association Membership Procedure — admission trigger, per-state account mapping, NCIGF and NOLHGA contact registration, annual roster-to-Schedule T reconciliation, policyholder summary-document delivery, and withdrawal run-off handling

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved jointly by the Head of Compliance and the Controller; re-approved each January and on any state guaranty act amendment, coverage-cap change or new state admission

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous obligation — membership is effective the day the certificate of authority issues, so the roster row must exist before the first policy is written in a state; the roster is reconciled to Annual Statement Schedule T before the March 1 statutory filing and association contacts are re-confirmed on each January data call

Deadline reminders configured.value: The licence register raises a membership task on every certificate-of-authority issuance and on each state continuation date, plus a January 15 reminder for the roster-to-Schedule T reconciliation and a reminder 10 days before each association data-call due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Membership confirmation letters, association contact registrations, per-state account mapping, data-call responses and the annual reconciliation retained 7 years after the certificate of authority for that state is surrendered

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any state carrying direct written premium with no mapped guaranty association membership, any unanswered association data call, and any undelivered life/health guaranty summary document is logged as an exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every missing-membership finding, every late association data-call response and every summary-document delivery gap before the exception is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state x line x writing-company combination holding a certificate of authority at any point in the calendar year, taken from the licence register and cross-checked to the direct-written-premium grid in Annual Statement Schedule T Part 1

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a state showing direct written premium on Schedule T with no mapped association membership and account is a fail; a data call answered after its due date or a coverage-cap change not reflected in the summary document is a fail; one or more fails escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs annually within 30 days of the March 1 Annual Statement filing, with an event-driven test inside 30 days of any new state admission, line addition or withdrawal

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain the licence register or the membership roster and must not have signed any association registration under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual guaranty association membership test workpaper (Schedule T extract, roster reconciliation, association confirmation letters, summary-document sample, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under the statement year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Membership roster with per-state account mapping, association confirmation letters, the Schedule T reconciliation and dated guaranty act captures, producible for an Alaska Division of Insurance financial examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns correspondence with the Division of Insurance and with each association; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that admits a lapsed membership or a missed data call before it is sent

checklist.step: Pull the live certificate-of-authority matrix by state, line and writing company
actions: In the licence register open Licences by Entity and export every certificate of authority with status Active, showing state, writing company, NAIC company code and each line of authority granted.
Ask the Statutory Reporting Manager for the prior-year Schedule T Part 1 direct-written-premium grid so states with premium but no active licence row surface immediately.
Flag any state where premium exists and the licence row is missing, expired or shows a line not on the certificate, and raise it to Regulatory Counsel the same day.
Save the export as guaranty-membership-base-<yyyy-mm-dd>.xlsx in the membership evidence folder.
checklist.done: an as-of-dated matrix exists showing every state, writing company and line of authority, reconciled against Schedule T premium.

checklist.step: Map each state and line to its guaranty association and assessment account
actions: For each P&C state row, name the property and casualty association (Alaska Insurance Guaranty Association under AS 21.80) and set the account: workers compensation, automobile, or all-other.

For each life, annuity or health row, name the life and health association (Alaska Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Association under AS 21.79) and set the account: life, annuity or health/disability.
Use the NCIGF member state pages for P&C associations and the NOLHGA state pages for life and health associations to confirm the legal name, administrator and mailing address of each association.
Record on each row the statutory account definition relied on and the date the association page was read.
Send the completed mapping to the Controller so the assessment register in the general ledger carries the same account structure.
checklist.done: every state and line row carries a named association, a statutory assessment account and a dated source reference.

checklist.step: Confirm membership is active with each association and register the company contacts
actions: Email each association administrator from the NCIGF or NOLHGA member contact page asking for written confirmation that each writing company is recorded as a member insurer, with the NAIC company code and accounts listed.

Register three named contacts with each association: assessment billing contact (Controller), data-call contact (Statutory Reporting Manager) and legal notice contact (Regulatory Counsel), with direct email and phone.
Where an association returns a mismatch (wrong NAIC code, missing account, dissolved company name), correct it in writing and keep the correction thread.
File every confirmation reply in the compliance evidence repository under <state>-membership-confirmation-<year>.
checklist.done: a written membership confirmation and three registered contacts exist for every association on the mapping.

checklist.step: Load the membership roster into the licence register as the system of record
actions: Create a Guaranty Association record against each certificate of authority holding association name, statutory cite, assessment account, membership effective date and the association contact block.
Attach the confirmation letter to the record so the evidence travels with the row.
Set the record owner to the Regulatory Affairs Manager and the reviewer to the Compliance Manager.
Run the built-in orphan report: certificates of authority with no guaranty association record, and association records with no live certificate.
checklist.done: the licence register returns zero orphans on both directions of the guaranty association orphan report.

checklist.step: Trigger membership set-up whenever a new certificate of authority is issued
actions: Add a mandatory task to the state expansion workflow: no state may be released for writing until its guaranty association record exists and the association has confirmed membership.
On receipt of a new certificate of authority from the Division of Insurance, create the association record the same week and email the association the new NAIC code and lines.
Tell the Insurance Product Manager the earliest write date only after the association confirmation lands, and record that date on the expansion plan.
Where a state grants a new line on an existing certificate, re-check whether it opens a new assessment account (adding workers compensation to a general-casualty licence does).
checklist.done: no state or line is released for writing without a confirmed association record dated before the first written policy.

checklist.step: Answer each association premium data call on time
actions: Log every association or NCIGF/NOLHGA data call on receipt with the association, the data requested, the measurement period and the stated due date.
Pull net direct written premium for the requested state, account and calendar year from the Annual Statement State Page (Exhibit of Premiums and Losses) and Schedule T, not from management reporting.
Tie the extracted figures to the filed statement line by line before releasing them, and have the Regulatory Reporting Analyst initial the tie-out.
Submit through the channel the association names (secure portal upload or signed PDF to the administrator) and keep the submission receipt.
Record the submission date against the due date in the data-call log.
checklist.done: every data call is answered on or before its due date with figures tied to the filed Annual Statement and a retained receipt.

checklist.step: Reconcile the roster to Schedule T and the State Page before the March 1 filing
actions: Export Schedule T Part 1 (direct business written by state) from the annual statement package for each writing company.
Join it to the guaranty association roster on state plus writing company and list any state with premium and no membership row.
Split premium into the assessable accounts using the State Page line-of-business detail so the workers compensation, automobile and all-other bases are separable when an assessment lands.
Give the Controller the resulting assessable-premium-by-account table as the forecasting base for the coming year.
Sign and date the reconciliation and file it before the March 1 statement filing.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation shows every premium-bearing state on Schedule T mapped to an active membership and an assessable-premium base by account.

checklist.step: Deliver the life and health guaranty association summary document with covered policies
actions: Confirm with Regulatory Counsel which states require the guaranty association summary document (the NOLHGA-style notice of coverage and limits) at delivery, at issue or at renewal, and the current dollar limits printed in each state version.
Load the state-specific summary document into the policy issuance package configuration so it is bundled automatically for every life, annuity and health policy in those states.
Run the issuance audit report monthly for policies issued without the required insert and re-mail within 10 business days.
Version-control each state summary document with an edition date and retire superseded editions in the document repository so no stale coverage limit can be issued.
checklist.done: every life, annuity and health policy issued in a notice state ships with the current-edition summary document, and the monthly gap report is cleared.

checklist.step: Police the statutory ban on using guaranty association coverage in sales material
actions: Add a mandatory review point to the advertising approval checklist: material may not use the existence of a guaranty association to induce a purchase, which the state acts prohibit outside the prescribed summary document.
Search approved sales collateral, agent presentations and web pages for the phrases guaranty association, guaranty fund and state-backed, and route every hit to Regulatory Counsel.
Where a hit is confirmed, withdraw the piece, issue a corrected version and notify the distribution channel that circulated it.
Brief the agency force through the agent portal bulletin each time the wording rules change.
checklist.done: no live sales or advertising material references guaranty association protection outside the prescribed summary document, evidenced by the dated collateral scan.

checklist.step: Track guaranty act amendments and coverage-limit changes by state
actions: Subscribe to the Division of Insurance bulletin feed for each of the 51 jurisdictions and to NCIGF and NOLHGA legislative trackers.

On each amendment, read the changed sections and record on the roster row what moved: covered lines, per-claim and aggregate coverage caps, assessment cap percentage, recoupment mechanism and the effective date.
Where a change affects the printed summary document or the recoupment method, raise a change request to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Controller within 5 business days.
Keep a dated PDF capture of the amended statutory text against the roster row as the evidence for the reading.
checklist.done: every act amendment in the period has a dated capture, a recorded impact on the roster row and a raised change request where downstream work is needed.

checklist.step: Keep the NCIGF and NOLHGA member profile and insolvency data readiness current
actions: Review the company profile held by NCIGF and NOLHGA each January: legal entity names, NAIC codes, group affiliation, licensed states and named contacts.
Confirm with the Claims Director / Manager that the claims platform can produce a Uniform Data Standard (UDS) claim extract if an association ever requests member data on an insolvency.
Diary the annual NCIGF and NOLHGA member communications so insolvency notices and assessment forecasts route straight to the Controller.
Correct any stale profile field in writing and keep the confirmation.
checklist.done: both member profiles are confirmed current for the year and a UDS-format extract has been proven producible from the claims platform.

checklist.step: Handle withdrawal, merger or line exit without dropping run-off membership
actions: On any planned surrender of a certificate of authority, confirm in writing with the association that membership obligations survive for business written while licensed, including assessments levied after the surrender date.
Keep the roster row open in run-off status with the surrender date recorded, rather than deleting it.
On a merger or novation, notify each association of the surviving NAIC code and the transferred premium so assessment bases follow the right entity.
Give the Controller the run-off state list so the assessment accrual model keeps those states in scope.
checklist.done: every surrendered or merged state remains on the roster in run-off status with written association acknowledgement of surviving obligations.

checklist.step: Report membership status and open association matters to the Compliance Committee
actions: Prepare a quarterly page: count of states by association type, new admissions and withdrawals in the quarter, open data calls, pending insolvencies notified by NCIGF/NOLHGA, and open membership exceptions with owners.
Show the assessable premium base by account alongside the statutory assessment cap so the committee sees the maximum annual exposure.
Table any act amendment that changes coverage caps or the recoupment mechanism.
Minute the committee decisions against each open exception.
checklist.done: a minuted quarterly committee item exists showing membership counts, open exceptions and maximum assessment exposure.

checklist.step: Log and remediate any state written without an active membership
actions: Raise an issue for each gap with the state, writing company, first policy effective date, premium written while unmapped and the account that should have applied.
Assign a root cause (expansion released before association confirmation, new line opened a new account, merger moved premium to an unregistered code) and an owner.
Contact the association immediately to register retroactively and ask in writing for the assessment history for the exposed period, then hand it to the Controller for accrual.
Set a remediation date and carry the issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every gap has an issue, a retroactive registration request, an accrual handoff, an owner and a remediation date.

checklist.step: File the membership evidence under the retention label
actions: Move the year folder (roster export, confirmation letters, data-call responses and receipts, Schedule T reconciliation, act captures) into the repository under Guaranty Association Membership / <year>.
Apply the retention label of 7 years from surrender of the certificate of authority so run-off states are not purged on a calendar rule.
Index each document by state, writing company, NAIC code and association name so an examiner request can be answered by state.
Confirm the repository access list gives read rights to Internal Audit and Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: the year folder is filed, labelled for retention past surrender and retrievable by state and NAIC code.

testing.step: Build the population of licensed state, line and company combinations
actions: Extract from the licence register every certificate of authority active at any point in the year, with state, writing company, NAIC code, lines of authority and effective/surrender dates.
Add every state showing direct written premium on Annual Statement Schedule T Part 1 for each writing company, so a premium-bearing unlicensed state cannot hide.
Add states in run-off (surrendered during or before the year with business still outstanding).
Reconcile the combined count to the licence register dashboard and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to both the licence register and Schedule T, and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the guaranty association roster
actions: Match each population row to a roster row on state plus writing company plus line.
Confirm the roster membership effective date is on or before the first policy effective date in that state, taken from the policy administration platform.
List unmatched rows, late-dated memberships and rows whose assessment account does not match the lines actually written as automatic exceptions.
Confirm run-off states remain on the roster rather than having been deleted at surrender.
testing.done: every population row matches an active or run-off roster row with an effective date preceding first written premium, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of states admitted, withdrawn or merged during the year, and 100% of run-off states.
Take 25 further rows at random using a recorded seed from the remaining population, for a minimum of 40 rows.
Record the seed, the population size, the extraction date and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note which rows are P&C and which are life and health, as the re-performance steps differ.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is documented covering all admissions, withdrawals, mergers and run-off states.

testing.step: Re-perform the association and account mapping against the statute
actions: For each sampled row, open the state guaranty act (for the Alaska rows, AS 21.80 for P&C and AS 21.79 for life and health) and read the member-insurer and account definitions as they stood in the year under test.
Reach your own conclusion on the association and assessment account before opening the roster row.
Compare to the recorded mapping; a right association with a wrong account is still an exception, because it drives the wrong assessment base.
Capture the statutory text page into the workpaper as the evidence for your conclusion.
testing.done: each sampled row carries an independent mapping conclusion, a captured statutory page and a comparison note.

testing.step: Trace each sampled membership to written association confirmation
actions: Open the confirmation letter filed against each sampled roster row and check it names the correct legal entity and NAIC company code.
Confirm the accounts listed by the association match the lines actually written per the State Page.
Confirm the three registered contacts (assessment billing, data call, legal notice) are current employees, by checking against the HR directory.
Treat an undated confirmation, a confirmation naming a superseded entity, or a contact who has left as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled row traces to a dated confirmation naming the right entity, code, accounts and current contacts.

testing.step: Re-perform the data-call responses against the filed statement
actions: Take every association data call logged in the year and pull the response actually submitted plus its receipt.
Re-extract net direct written premium for the same state, account and period from the filed Annual Statement State Page and Schedule T.
Compare the re-extracted figure to the submitted figure and quantify any variance in dollars and percent.
Compare the submission date to the association due date and count the days late where applicable.
testing.done: every data call is re-performed with a quantified variance and a days-late count, and unsupported figures are logged.

testing.step: Test the life and health summary-document delivery on issued policies
actions: Draw 25 life, annuity and health policies issued in notice states during the year from the policy administration issue register.
Open the archived issue package in the document repository and confirm the state guaranty association summary document is present.
Compare the printed coverage limits on the delivered edition against the limits in the state act as at the issue date.
Treat a missing insert, a superseded edition or a stale coverage limit as separate exception types.
testing.done: each sampled policy shows a present, current-edition summary document with limits matching the act at issue date, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Test admissions and withdrawals for timing breaks
actions: For each state admitted during the year, compare the association confirmation date to the first policy effective date in that state from the policy administration platform.
Any premium written before the confirmation date is a reportable compliance breach, not a documentation exception.
For each withdrawal or merger, confirm written association acknowledgement that assessment obligations survive for business written while licensed, and that the roster row remained open in run-off.
Recompute the exposed premium for any break as the direct written premium between the first policy date and the confirmation date.
testing.done: every admission and withdrawal is timing-tested, with exposed premium quantified for any break.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying state, writing company, exception type, exposed premium and the compliance impact.

Assign a root cause (expansion released ahead of confirmation, new line opened an unmapped account, merger moved premium to an unregistered NAIC code, data call missed, stale summary-document edition) and a named owner.
For premium-written-before-membership breaks, open a retroactive registration request with the association and a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Set a remediation date and carry every open issue into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sample and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for unmapped premium-bearing states.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each supporting point.
Have the Internal Auditor, who neither maintains the licence register nor signed any registration under test, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any premium-written-before-membership breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under the statement year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns assessment validation, SSAP No. 35R accrual, payment authorisation and the recoupment asset; premium-tax offset execution delegated to the Tax Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the assessment, cap and recoupment sections of Alaska AS 21.80 (P&C) and AS 21.79 (life and health) read at each assessment; parallel sections confirmed for Arizona (A.R.S. Title 20, Ch. 3), California (Ins. Code section 1063.5 assessment and section 1063.14 recoupment surcharge) and Colorado (C.R.S. Title 10, Art. 4, Part 5), together with SSAP No. 35R for accounting recognition

In-scope processes.value: Assessment notice intake, base and cap validation against filed statutory premium, SSAP No. 35R liability accrual, payment on the notice due date, recoupment through premium-tax offset or policyholder surcharge, and Annual Statement Note 14 disclosure — every Class A administrative and Class B insolvency assessment across 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Assessment register, accrual and recoupment asset are booked in the general ledger by state, association and account; the filed premium base comes from the statutory reporting system and payments run through accounts payable

Compliance procedure documented.value: Guaranty Association Assessment Procedure — notice intake and register entry, class and legal-basis validation, base recomputation from the State Page, statutory cap test, SSAP No. 35R accrual and recoupment asset, payment authorisation, tax-offset claim and Note 14 disclosure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer on the Controller recommendation; re-approved annually at year-end close and on any change to a state assessment cap, offset percentage or SSAP No. 35R guidance

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per assessment — payment is due on the date stated in the association notice, commonly 30 days from the notice date; the accrual must land in the quarter the insolvency triggering it occurred; the premium-tax offset is claimed on the state return (Alaska annual return due March 1) and Note 14 disclosure lands with the March 1 Annual Statement

Deadline reminders configured.value: Assessment register raises reminders at notice date plus 5 days (validation complete), 10 days before the payment due date, at each quarter-end close for accrual review, and 30 days before each state premium-tax return due date for the offset claim

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Assessment notice, base recomputation, cap test, accrual journal, remittance advice and proof of payment, offset claim and association acknowledgement retained 7 years from the year the recoupment is fully recovered

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late payment, an assessment paid without a base recomputation and cap test, an un-recouped offset that expired, and an unaccrued known insolvency are each logged as exceptions with root cause, dollar impact and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off any late or overpaid assessment, any write-off of an unrecovered recoupment asset and any restatement of the Note 14 disclosure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every guaranty association assessment notice received in the period across all associations and writing companies, joined to the general ledger assessment expense and liability accounts and to the recoupment asset roll-forward

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on late payment and on assessments exceeding the statutory cap; base recomputation must agree to the filed State Page within 0.5% or the variance must be evidenced by a written association explanation; any expired unrecovered offset above $25,000 escalates to the Chief Financial Officer

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per assessment; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's notices with 100% coverage of Class B insolvency assessments, plus an annual test of the recoupment asset roll-forward at year-end close

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or approved any sampled accrual, payment or offset claim

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly assessment test workpaper (notice log, base recomputations, cap tests, payment traces, offset roll-forward, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the close binder in the financial reporting repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Assessment register export with per-notice base, cap test, payment proof and offset status, tied to Note 14 of the Annual Statement, producible for a Division of Insurance financial examination or a state tax audit within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Controller answers association billing queries; the Tax Manager answers state revenue-department queries on the offset claim; Regulatory Counsel clears any position disputing an assessment before it is sent to the association

checklist.step: Intake the assessment notice and open a register entry
actions: Route all association mail to the registered assessment billing mailbox so no notice lands in an individual inbox.

Open an assessment register entry capturing association, state, writing company and NAIC code, notice date, class (A administrative or B insolvency), the named insolvent estate, assessment account, base year, rate applied, amount due and payment due date.
Scan the notice and attach it to the register entry the day it arrives.
Notify the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Tax Manager the same day so the base recomputation and the offset planning start together.
checklist.done: the register entry exists with all notice fields populated and the scanned notice attached, dated the day of receipt.

checklist.step: Validate the assessment class and legal basis against the state act
actions: Read the assessment sections of the state act (for Alaska, AS 21.80 for P&C and AS 21.79 for life and health) and confirm the class levied is authorised: Class A for administrative expenses, Class B for the obligations of a specific insolvent member.
Confirm the company was a member insurer writing in the named account during the period the insolvency arose, using the run-off-aware membership roster.
Confirm the insolvency is a covered event: an order of liquidation with a finding of insolvency entered by the domiciliary court, not merely a rehabilitation or a supervision order.
Record the statutory cite, the liquidation order date and the court on the register entry, and flag any assessment for a period the company did not write.
checklist.done: the register entry names the authorising statutory section, the liquidation order and its date, and confirms member status for the assessed period.

checklist.step: Recompute the assessment base from the filed statutory premium
actions: Identify the base year the notice uses (normally net direct written premium for the calendar year preceding the assessment) and the account it applies to.

Pull that premium from the filed Annual Statement State Page (Exhibit of Premiums and Losses by State) and Schedule T for the named state and writing company, restricted to the lines in the assessed account.
Recompute the base and compare to the base printed on the notice; quantify any variance in dollars and percent.
Where the variance exceeds 0.5%, write to the association administrator with the State Page extract and ask for the source of their figure before paying.
Attach the recomputation worksheet to the register entry.
checklist.done: the assessment base is recomputed from filed statutory premium and either agrees within 0.5% or has a written association explanation attached.

checklist.step: Test the levy against the statutory assessment cap
actions: Read the cap in the state act (commonly 2% of net direct written premium in that account for the base year, per account, per calendar year) and record the exact percentage on the register entry.
Sum all assessments already levied by that association on that account in the same calendar year, including the current notice.
Compute cap headroom = base x cap percentage minus assessments to date, and record whether the current notice fits.
Where the notice breaches the cap, hold payment, notify the Controller and Regulatory Counsel the same day and query the association in writing.
Where the cap is reached, record the deferred balance the association is entitled to levy in later years so the forecast carries it.
checklist.done: a cap test showing base, cap percentage, year-to-date assessments and headroom is attached, and any breach is held and queried before payment.

checklist.step: Query or dispute a defective assessment before the due date
actions: Where the base, the account, the assessed entity or the cap test fails, send a written query to the association administrator naming the specific defect and attaching the recomputation.
Ask explicitly whether the due date is extended pending resolution, and pay the undisputed portion on the original due date regardless.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any letter that disputes liability rather than arithmetic before it leaves.
Log the query, the response and the resolution on the register entry with dates.
checklist.done: each defect has a dated written query, the undisputed amount is paid on time, and the resolution is recorded.

checklist.step: Accrue the liability under SSAP No. 35R
actions: Apply SSAP No. 35R: recognise the liability when the insolvency has occurred, the assessment is probable and reasonably estimable, and premium giving rise to the assessment has been written.

For known insolvencies not yet assessed, estimate the future assessment from the NCIGF or NOLHGA estimate of estate shortfall multiplied by the company market share in the affected account, and accrue it.
Post the accrual journal to the guaranty fund assessment liability account with the state, association and estate carried in the analysis dimensions.
Attach the estimate support and have the Controller approve the journal before posting.
Roll the accrual forward at each quarter-end close and true it up against notices actually received.
checklist.done: the liability is posted with SSAP No. 35R support, analysed by state, association and estate, and reviewed at each quarter-end close.

checklist.step: Recognise the recoupment asset for premium-tax offset or policyholder surcharge
actions: For each assessed state, confirm from the act whether recoupment is by premium-tax offset, by policyholder surcharge, or not permitted, and record the mechanism on the register entry.
Where offset applies, record the schedule the state allows (commonly 20% of the assessment per year over five years, beginning the year after payment) and the expiry date of the unused balance.
Recognise the recoupment asset only to the extent recovery is probable against forecast premium-tax liability in that state, per SSAP No. 35R, and document the forecast used.
Where the state permits no recoupment, expense the assessment in full and note the reason on the register entry.
Maintain a recoupment roll-forward by state and assessment year: opening balance, additions, amounts claimed, expiries and closing balance.
checklist.done: each assessment carries a named recoupment mechanism, a claim schedule with expiry dates, and a roll-forward line supported by a premium-tax forecast.

checklist.step: Authorise and release payment before the notice due date
actions: Raise the payment request against the register entry only after the base recomputation, cap test and legal-basis validation are all marked complete.
Set up or confirm the association as an approved payee with bank details verified by callback to the administrator using the number on the NCIGF or NOLHGA member page, never the number on the notice.
Schedule the payment to clear at least 3 business days before the notice due date and use the remittance reference the notice specifies (estate name and assessment number).
Attach the payment confirmation and the remittance advice to the register entry and set the entry status to Paid.
checklist.done: cleared funds and a remittance advice are attached, dated on or before the notice due date, with payee bank details independently verified.

checklist.step: Book the payment, clear the accrual and reconcile the liability account
actions: Post the payment against the guaranty fund assessment liability, clearing the specific accrual rather than the pooled balance.
Reconcile the liability account each month: opening accrual, new accruals, payments, true-ups, closing balance, tied line by line to the assessment register.
Investigate and clear any reconciling item older than 60 days and escalate unresolved items to the Controller.
File the signed reconciliation in the close binder for the period.
checklist.done: the liability account reconciles to the assessment register with no reconciling item older than 60 days, and the reconciliation is signed.

checklist.step: Claim the premium-tax offset on the state return
actions: Take the eligible offset instalment for the return year from the recoupment roll-forward for each state.

Enter it on the guaranty association assessment credit line of the state premium-tax return and attach the schedule the state requires (assessment notice copy, proof of payment, prior claims to date).

File through the state channel — NAIC OPTins where the state accepts it, otherwise the revenue department portal — and keep the submission confirmation; the Alaska annual premium-tax return is due March 1.
Reduce the recoupment asset by the amount claimed and record the confirmation number against the roll-forward line.
Escalate to the Controller any offset balance within one year of expiry that the forecast premium-tax liability cannot absorb.
checklist.done: each eligible instalment is claimed on a filed return with a confirmation number, and the recoupment asset is reduced accordingly.

checklist.step: Implement the policyholder recoupment surcharge where the state uses that mechanism
actions: Take from Regulatory Counsel the state-authorised surcharge percentage, the effective date and the recoupment window, plus the wording of the required policyholder notice.
Configure the surcharge as a separately stated charge on the declarations page and the billing statement for the affected state and lines, never buried in premium.
Track the amount collected against the assessment being recouped and stop the surcharge when the assessment is fully recovered, as the acts require.
File any surcharge notice or filing the state demands before first use, and keep the collected-versus-assessed reconciliation monthly.
checklist.done: the surcharge is separately stated, notified, reconciled monthly against the assessment recouped and stopped at full recovery.

checklist.step: Disclose the assessments in the Annual Statement Note 14 and the expense exhibits
actions: Prepare the Note 14 disclosure (Liabilities, Contingencies and Assessments): assets recognised for premium-tax offsets and policy surcharges, liabilities for assessments, and the related SSAP No. 35R roll-forward.
Tie the disclosed liability and asset balances to the assessment register and the recoupment roll-forward before the note is released.
Confirm the assessment expense is classified in the correct expense line of the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit and mapped for the Risk-Based Capital filing.
Have the Controller review and initial the note against the supporting schedules ahead of the March 1 filing.
checklist.done: Note 14 ties to the assessment register and recoupment roll-forward and is initialled by the Controller before the March 1 filing.

checklist.step: Complete the post-assessment data reporting the association requires
actions: Answer the association follow-on data requests (net direct written premium by account, policy counts, recoupment amounts collected) using filed statutory figures only.
Where the state requires an annual report of surcharge amounts collected and remitted, prepare it on the state form and file it by the stated date.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager tie every figure to the filed statement before release and initial the tie-out.
Keep the submission receipt and record the submission date against the due date.
checklist.done: each post-assessment report is filed by its due date with a tie-out to filed statutory figures and a retained receipt.

checklist.step: Forecast future assessments from insolvency notices and market share
actions: Track every new liquidation order circulated by NCIGF and NOLHGA and identify the affected states, lines and accounts.
Estimate the company share as its net direct written premium in the affected account and state, divided by the industry total for that account, applied to the estimated estate shortfall.
Compare each state estimate against remaining annual cap headroom to spread the exposure over the years the association can legally levy.
Give the forecast to the Controller for the SSAP No. 35R accrual and to the Chief Financial Officer for the capital and expense plan each quarter.
checklist.done: a quarterly forecast exists per open insolvency showing estimated exposure, cap-constrained timing and the accrual handoff.

checklist.step: Retain assessment evidence for the full retention period
actions: File per assessment: notice, legal-basis validation, base recomputation, cap test, accrual journal, payment proof, offset claims and association acknowledgements.
Apply a retention label of 7 years from the year the recoupment is fully recovered, so records survive a five-year offset schedule plus audit reach-back.
Index by state, association, estate name, assessment number and payment date so a tax audit query can be answered by estate.
Give the Tax Manager and Internal Audit standing read access to the folder.
checklist.done: every assessment folder is complete, labelled for retention past full recoupment and retrievable by estate and assessment number.

testing.step: Build the population of assessments received in the period
actions: Export every assessment register entry with a notice date in the period, showing association, state, writing company, class, estate, amount and due date.
Independently extract all postings to the guaranty fund assessment expense and liability accounts and all payments to association payees in the same period.
Add insolvencies circulated by NCIGF and NOLHGA in the period that carry no register entry, so an unaccrued known insolvency cannot hide.
Reconcile the three sources and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles the register, the ledger and the insolvency notices, and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile register entries to ledger accruals and payments
actions: Match each register entry to its accrual journal and its payment posting on state plus association plus estate.
List register entries with no accrual, ledger postings with no register entry, and payments that do not clear a specific accrual.
Agree the closing liability balance to the sum of unpaid register entries and investigate the difference to the dollar.
Agree the closing recoupment asset to the roll-forward closing balance.
testing.done: register, ledger, liability balance and recoupment roll-forward are reconciled with every difference explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Class B insolvency assessments and 100% of assessments above $250,000.
Take 15 further notices at random using a recorded seed from the remaining Class A population, for a minimum of 25 items.
Record the seed, population size, extraction date and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add every insolvency notice with no register entry as a mandatory 100% item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is documented covering all Class B assessments, all large items and all unregistered insolvencies.

testing.step: Re-perform the assessment base from the filed statutory premium
actions: For each sampled notice, open the filed Annual Statement State Page and Schedule T for the base year, state and writing company named on the notice.
Sum net direct written premium for only the lines belonging to the assessed account and reach your own base figure before opening the preparer worksheet.
Compare your base to both the notice base and the preparer recomputation, and quantify each variance in dollars and percent against the 0.5% threshold.
Capture the State Page extract into the workpaper as the source for your figure.
testing.done: each sampled notice has an independent base figure, two quantified variances and a captured State Page extract.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory cap test
actions: Read the cap percentage directly from the state act for each sampled state rather than from the register entry.
Recompute maximum annual assessment = your independent base x the statutory cap percentage, per account.
Sum all assessments levied by that association on that account in the same calendar year and confirm the total sits inside the cap.
Any assessment paid above the cap is a recoverable overpayment, not a test exception, and is quantified and referred to the Controller for recovery.
testing.done: each sampled account has an independently recomputed cap, a year-to-date total inside it, or a quantified overpayment referred for recovery.

testing.step: Trace payment timing and payee integrity
actions: For each sampled notice, open the payment posting and read the value date on the bank confirmation.
Compute days early or late against the notice due date and list every late payment with the amount and the days late.
Confirm the payee bank details on file match the association details independently obtained from the NCIGF or NOLHGA member page, and that a callback verification is evidenced.
Confirm the payment cleared the specific accrual rather than a pooled balance.
testing.done: every sampled payment has a value date compared to the due date and independently verified payee details.

testing.step: Test the SSAP No. 35R accrual recognition and completeness
actions: For each liquidation order circulated in the period, confirm an accrual exists in the quarter the insolvency occurred, not the quarter the notice arrived.

Re-perform the estimate for two large open insolvencies: company net direct written premium in the affected account and state, divided by the industry account total, applied to the published estate shortfall estimate.
Compare your estimate to the booked accrual and explain any difference above 10%.
Treat a known liquidation with premium written in the affected account and no accrual as a completeness failure.
testing.done: every liquidation order in the period maps to an accrual in the correct quarter, with two re-performed estimates documented.

testing.step: Test the recoupment asset and offset claims
actions: Take the recoupment roll-forward and vouch each addition to a paid assessment and each reduction to a filed premium-tax return line and confirmation number.
Recompute the annual instalment against the state schedule (commonly 20% per year over five years from the year after payment) and check the expiry date carried on each line.
For surcharge states, agree amounts collected in the billing system to the assessment being recouped and confirm collection stopped at full recovery.
List any balance expiring within twelve months that the premium-tax forecast cannot absorb, and quantify the write-off exposure.
testing.done: every roll-forward movement is vouched, instalments and expiries are recomputed, and expiring unrecoverable balances are quantified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying association, state, estate, exception type and the dollar impact.

Assign a root cause (notice reached an individual mailbox, base taken from management rather than filed premium, cap test skipped, accrual deferred to notice receipt, offset instalment missed) and a named owner.
For overpayments and expired offsets, open a recovery action with the association or the state revenue department and name the recovery owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open issue into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, a dollar impact, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance thresholds on late payment and cap breach.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each supporting point, and state the total dollar impact of exceptions.
Have the Internal Auditor, who prepared and approved none of the sampled accruals, payments or offset claims, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any cap breaches and any expiring recoupment balances to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper with the close binder reference.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate, dollar impact and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns servicing of residual-market assigned policies and of policies administered at a guaranty association direction; underwriting judgement escalates to the Underwriting Director / Manager, claim judgement to the Claims Director / Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the servicing and continuation-of-coverage sections of Alaska AS 21.80 (P&C guaranty association) and AS 21.79 (life and health), read alongside the plan documents that actually govern day-to-day servicing: the NCCI-administered assigned risk plan rules and Assigned Carrier / Servicing Carrier Performance Standards, and the AIPSO manual of rules for the automobile plan; parallel provisions confirmed for Arizona, California and Colorado

In-scope processes.value: Assignment intake, policy issuance, plan-rate application, billing and collection, premium audit, cancellation and nonrenewal, and claim handling for every residual-market assigned policy, plus administration of policies of an insolvent member insurer where the guaranty association designates the company to service them — 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Assigned policies are issued, rated and endorsed on the policy administration platform under a dedicated residual-market product code; claims are handled on the claims platform under a plan-flagged claim type, and plan reporting extracts are drawn from both

Compliance procedure documented.value: Residual Market Servicing Procedure — assignment intake and acknowledgement, issuance timeliness standard, plan-rate-only rating, plan cancellation grounds and notice periods, premium audit turnaround, claim contact standards, plan data reporting and pool settlement

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Operating Officer with the Underwriting Director / Manager and Claims Director / Manager as co-approvers; re-approved annually and on any plan rule circular or performance-standard revision

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous obligation with plan-set clocks: bind on the assignment effective date, issue the policy within the plan issuance standard (30 days of assignment is the working standard), first claim contact within 24 hours of notice, premium audit completed within 90 days of expiration and billed within 30 days of audit, unit statistical report due 18 months after policy effective date, and monthly pool settlement reporting

Deadline reminders configured.value: Workflow SLAs on the assignment queue at day 3 (acknowledged), day 20 (issuance at risk) and day 30 (issuance breach), audit queue alerts at 60 and 85 days post-expiration, claim contact alerts at 12 and 20 hours, and a calendar entry for each unit statistical and pool reporting due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Assignment notices, issued policy and endorsements, rating worksheets showing plan rates, audit workpapers, cancellation and nonrenewal notices with proof of mailing, claim files and plan data submissions retained 7 years after final policy expiration or final claim closure, whichever is later

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Issuance beyond the plan standard, any deviation from plan-filed rates, a cancellation on a ground the plan does not allow, a missed audit window and a late plan data submission are each logged as exceptions with root cause, affected policy numbers and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every plan performance-standard breach, every reinstatement following an improper cancellation and every corrective action plan filed with the plan administrator

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All residual-market assigned policies in force or issued during the quarter under the plan product code, all cancellations and nonrenewals on those policies, all premium audits due in the quarter and all claims reported on assigned policies

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Plan performance standards are the thresholds: issuance within 30 days of assignment at 95% or better, premium audits completed within 90 days of expiration at 90% or better, first claim contact inside 24 hours at 95% or better; zero tolerance on off-plan rating and on cancellation for a ground the plan does not permit

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs quarterly across the quarter population, with 100% review of cancellations and nonrenewals and a targeted test ahead of any scheduled plan servicing-carrier performance audit

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the residual-market servicing unit and must not have underwritten, audited or adjusted any sampled policy or claim

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly residual-market servicing test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, rating recomputations, timeliness statistics, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under the plan and quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Servicing statistics against each plan performance standard, sampled policy and claim files, plan data submission receipts and pool settlement reconciliations, producible for a plan servicing-carrier performance audit or a Division of Insurance market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Operations Manager owns responses to the plan administrator (NCCI or AIPSO) and to the guaranty association; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns Division of Insurance inquiries, with Regulatory Counsel clearing any admission of a servicing-standard breach

checklist.step: Load the current plan rules and servicing carrier performance standards
actions: Download from the plan administrator site the current plan manual for each state the company services (NCCI assigned risk plan rules for workers compensation, the AIPSO manual of rules for the automobile plan) and the applicable Servicing Carrier or Assigned Carrier Performance Standards.

Extract into a one-page state standards card: issuance days, binding rules, allowed cancellation grounds and notice days, audit turnaround, claim contact and reserve-setting standards, and reporting due dates.
Diff the new manual against the prior edition and list every changed rule with its effective date.
Circulate the changed-rules list to Underwriting, Billing, Premium Audit and Claims leads and file the manual with an edition date in the repository.
checklist.done: a current, edition-dated standards card exists per state with a circulated diff of changes against the prior edition.

checklist.step: Take in the assignment from the plan administrator and acknowledge it
actions: Pull the daily assignment file from the plan administrator portal and load each assignment into the residual-market queue with assignment number, insured, state, effective date and assignment term.
Acknowledge receipt to the plan administrator within the acknowledgement window stated in the standards card, normally 3 business days.
Check the assignment against the plan eligibility record: the risk must have been rejected by the voluntary market and must not already be assigned to another carrier.
Where the assignment is defective (duplicate, wrong state, ineligible class), reject it back to the administrator in writing inside the rejection window rather than issuing.
Bind coverage effective on the assignment effective date so there is no gap while issuance completes.
checklist.done: every assignment is loaded, acknowledged inside the window, eligibility-checked, and either bound on its effective date or formally rejected.

checklist.step: Issue the assigned policy within the plan issuance standard
actions: Create the policy under the residual-market product code so plan rules, forms and rates apply and the policy is excluded from voluntary reporting.
Attach only plan-approved forms and endorsements for the state and the assigned classification; no voluntary-market endorsement may be added.
Issue and mail within the plan issuance standard (30 days of assignment as the working standard) and record the issuance date against the assignment date in the queue.
Where issuance will breach, escalate to the Operations Manager before day 20 with the reason and the expected date.
Send the issued policy to the producer of record shown on the assignment and to the insured at the address on the application.
checklist.done: the policy is issued under the plan product code with plan-only forms, inside the plan issuance standard or with a pre-breach escalation on file.

checklist.step: Rate the assigned risk on plan-filed rates only
actions: Rate from the plan-filed residual-market rate pages for the state and effective date, not from the company voluntary manual, and record the rate page edition on the rating worksheet.

Apply the mandatory plan modifiers in the order the manual sets them: experience modification from the rating bureau, any assigned risk adjustment or surcharge program the plan applies, and the state expense constant.
Take the experience modification from the rating bureau issuance rather than a broker-supplied figure, and record the mod effective date.
Do not apply schedule credits, discretionary credits or voluntary tiering; the plan does not permit them.
Save the rating worksheet showing rate pages, classifications, payroll or exposure basis, modifiers and the resulting premium to the policy file.
checklist.done: the rating worksheet shows plan rate pages, a bureau-issued modification and no discretionary credit, and the premium reproduces from those inputs.

checklist.step: Bill and collect on the plan payment rules
actions: Set the payment plan to a plan-permitted option only (the deposit percentage and instalment schedule stated in the plan manual) and record which option the insured elected.
Issue invoices on the plan schedule and apply the plan late-payment and reinstatement rules rather than the company voluntary rules.
Where a payment is missed, run the plan nonpayment sequence: the plan notice of intent, the statutory notice period, and the cancellation date, all logged with proof of mailing.
Reconcile collected premium to the policy premium each month and hand the plan-attributable balances to the Reinsurance Accountant for pool settlement.
checklist.done: billing runs on a plan-permitted payment option with the plan nonpayment sequence evidenced and monthly premium reconciled for pool settlement.

checklist.step: Complete the premium audit inside the plan turnaround standard
actions: Queue every assigned policy for audit at expiration and select the audit type the plan requires for the premium size (physical audit above the plan threshold, otherwise mail or telephone audit).

Obtain payroll records, tax filings and the general ledger detail from the insured, verify classification assignment against the rating bureau scopes manual, and document any class change with the basis.
Complete the audit within 90 days of expiration and bill or return the audit premium within 30 days of audit completion, per the plan standard.
Where the insured refuses access or records, follow the plan noncompliance route: issue the estimated audit at the plan multiplier and notify the plan administrator.
File the audit workpapers, the signed audit statement and the billing to the policy file.
checklist.done: each audit is completed within 90 days of expiration, billed within 30 days of completion, and evidenced by signed workpapers or a documented noncompliance route.

checklist.step: Cancel or nonrenew only on plan-permitted grounds and notice periods
actions: Before any cancellation, check the state standards card for the permitted grounds, which in residual market plans are limited (nonpayment, fraud or material misrepresentation, refusal of audit or inspection, and the plan-specific grounds), and record which ground applies.
Apply the longer of the plan notice period and the statutory notice period for the state, and send by the method the state requires, keeping proof of mailing or certificate of bulk mailing.
Copy the plan administrator, the producer of record and any statutory notice recipient (mortgagee, loss payee, or the state fund where required).
Where a cancellation is later found to be on an unpermitted ground, reinstate flat, restore coverage from inception and log the event as an exception.
For nonrenewal, confirm the plan actually permits nonrenewal of an assigned risk rather than requiring re-assignment, and follow the re-assignment route where it does.
checklist.done: every cancellation and nonrenewal names a plan-permitted ground, uses the longer notice period, and carries proof of mailing and administrator copy.

checklist.step: Handle claims on assigned policies to the plan claim standards
actions: Flag every claim on a residual-market policy with the plan claim type so plan handling standards and plan reporting apply automatically.
Enforce the plan contact standard: contact the claimant, the employer or insured and the treating provider within 24 hours of notice, and record each contact with a timestamp.
Set reserves to the plan reserve-adequacy standard within the plan timeframe and re-evaluate on the plan review cycle, since pool members fund the outcome.
Refer claims above the plan authority threshold to the plan administrator for consent before settlement, and file the consent in the claim file.
Apply the plan large-loss reporting rule: report claims exceeding the plan reporting threshold to the administrator inside the stated days.
checklist.done: each plan-flagged claim shows timestamped 24-hour contacts, plan-standard reserving, and administrator consent or notification where thresholds are crossed.

checklist.step: Administer policies of an insolvent member insurer where the association designates the company
actions: On receipt of a designation from the guaranty association or the liquidator, load the transferred block under a separate administration code that records the estate name, the liquidation order date and the association as the funding party.

Apply the statutory continuation rule from the state act: coverage continues only to the earlier of the policy expiration, the date the policyholder replaces it, or the statutory cut-off after the liquidation order (commonly 30 days), and issue the statutory notice of termination on that basis.

Cap benefits and claim payments at the state statutory limits (the per-claim cap and any deductible the act imposes) rather than the insolvent insurer policy limits, and record the cap applied on each claim.
Produce claim and policy data to the association in the Uniform Data Standard (UDS) format on the association reporting cycle, and reconcile reimbursements received against payments made.
Tell policyholders in writing how to file a claim against the estate before the liquidation bar date set by the court.
checklist.done: the designated block is administered under its own code with statutory continuation dates, statutory caps applied per claim, UDS reporting delivered and reimbursements reconciled.

checklist.step: Report unit statistical and financial data to the plan administrator
actions: Build the unit statistical report from the policy and claim systems for each assigned policy and submit through the plan administrator data channel (NCCI Data Manager for workers compensation, the AIPSO reporting channel for the automobile plan).

Meet the reporting clocks: first unit statistical report due 18 months after policy effective date with subsequent reports on the annual cycle, and the annual financial calls due on the administrator schedule.
Run the administrator edit package before submission and clear every critical edit rather than submitting with rejects.
Reconcile reported premium and losses to the general ledger and to the pool settlement statements, and hand differences to the Reinsurance Accountant.
Keep the submission acknowledgement and the edit-clear report against each due date.
checklist.done: every unit statistical and financial submission is filed by its due date with critical edits cleared and reconciled to the ledger.

checklist.step: Settle pool balances and servicing allowances with the plan
actions: Prepare the monthly plan settlement: premium written and collected, losses and allocated expenses paid, and the servicing carrier allowance calculated at the plan allowance percentage on the correct premium base.
Cede the assigned business to the pool in the ceded accounting platform under the plan treaty code so the residual-market result is not mingled with voluntary reinsurance.
Agree the administrator settlement statement line by line to the company submission and clear differences before remitting or claiming the balance.
Escalate any unagreed balance older than 60 days to the Controller and the plan administrator in writing.
checklist.done: the monthly settlement is agreed to the administrator statement with the allowance recomputed and no unagreed balance older than 60 days.

checklist.step: Handle complaints and plan escalations on assigned business
actions: Tag every complaint on an assigned policy as residual market so it is answered against plan rules and counted separately in market conduct reporting.

Answer Division of Insurance complaints within the state response deadline (commonly 10 to 21 days from the department letter) and copy the plan administrator where the complaint concerns plan servicing.
Where the complaint alleges off-plan rating, improper cancellation or issuance delay, open a servicing exception at the same time as the response so the root cause is fixed, not just answered.
Feed the complaint counts and causes into the quarterly servicing performance pack.
checklist.done: every residual-market complaint is tagged, answered inside the state deadline, copied to the administrator where relevant, and linked to a servicing exception where a rule was broken.

checklist.step: Track servicing performance against each plan standard monthly
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard measuring the exact plan metrics: percent issued within the issuance standard, percent audited within 90 days of expiration, percent of claims contacted inside 24 hours, unit statistical submission timeliness and critical-edit rate.
Show each metric against the plan performance standard threshold and the trend over twelve months.
Where a metric falls below standard for two consecutive months, open a corrective action with a named owner before the administrator raises it.
Circulate the dashboard to the Underwriting Director / Manager, Claims Director / Manager and the Chief Operating Officer.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard exists measuring every plan standard, with corrective actions opened on any two-month miss.

checklist.step: Prepare for and clear the plan servicing carrier performance audit
actions: On notice of a plan performance audit, assemble the requested file population and pre-review a sample against the same performance standards the auditor will apply.
Fix and document any file defect found in pre-review (missing rating worksheet, absent proof of mailing, undocumented class change) before the auditor arrives.
Host the audit, log every finding with the plan citation the auditor relies on, and agree the factual record before the exit meeting.
Write the corrective action plan with owners and dates, submit it to the administrator inside the response window, and track it to closure.
checklist.done: the audit closes with an agreed factual record and a submitted corrective action plan tracked to closure.

checklist.step: Retain servicing records for the full retention period
actions: File per policy: assignment notice and acknowledgement, issued policy and endorsements, rating worksheet, billing history, audit workpapers, cancellation or nonrenewal notice with proof of mailing, and plan submissions.
File per claim: notice, contact log, reserve history, administrator consents and settlement documents, under the plan claim type.
Apply the retention label of 7 years after final policy expiration or final claim closure, whichever is later, so open claims cannot trigger an early purge.
Index by assignment number, policy number, state and plan so an administrator audit request can be answered by assignment number.
checklist.done: policy and claim records are filed, retention-labelled to the later of expiration or claim closure, and retrievable by assignment number.

testing.step: Build the population of assigned policies, audits and claims for the quarter
actions: Extract every policy under the residual-market product code in force or issued in the quarter, with assignment number, assignment date, issuance date, state, effective and expiration dates.
Extract all cancellations and nonrenewals on those policies, all premium audits due in the quarter, and all claims reported on plan-flagged policies.
Reconcile the policy count to the assignment files received from the plan administrator for the quarter, so an assignment issued outside the plan product code cannot hide.
Add the designated insolvent-insurer block administered for the guaranty association as a separate population stratum.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the administrator assignment files and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the plan administrator records
actions: Match each administrator assignment to a bound policy on assignment number and effective date.
List assignments with no policy, policies with no assignment, and policies bound after the assignment effective date, as automatic exceptions.
Compare the plan-reported in-force count and premium to the internal extract and explain any variance above 1%.
Confirm every rejected assignment carries a written rejection sent inside the plan rejection window.
testing.done: every administrator assignment maps to a bound policy or a timely written rejection, with variances explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of cancellations and nonrenewals and 100% of policies from the designated insolvent-insurer block.
Take 30 policies at random using a recorded seed from the remaining in-force population, plus 15 premium audits and 15 plan-flagged claims.
Record the seed, the population sizes, the extraction date and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Stratify the policy sample by state so at least one policy is drawn from every state serviced in the quarter.
testing.done: a reproducible, state-stratified sample is documented covering all cancellations and the full insolvent-insurer block.

testing.step: Re-perform the rating on plan-filed rates for each sampled policy
actions: Open the plan-filed residual-market rate pages in force at the policy effective date and rate the risk independently from the classifications and exposures on the application.
Take the experience modification directly from the rating bureau issuance and confirm the mod effective date matches the policy term.
Compare your premium to the issued premium and treat any variance above $1 that is not explained by a plan-mandated modifier as an off-plan rating exception.
Check specifically for schedule credits, discretionary credits or voluntary tier factors, which the plan does not permit, and flag any hit as a zero-tolerance fail.
Capture the rate page and the bureau mod sheet into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled policy has an independently recomputed premium with any variance explained by a plan-mandated modifier or logged as a fail.

testing.step: Recompute the issuance, audit and claim-contact timeliness statistics
actions: Recompute days from assignment date to issuance date for the whole population and derive the percent inside the 30-day plan standard.
Recompute days from policy expiration to audit completion and from audit completion to billing, and derive the percent inside the 90-day and 30-day standards.
Recompute hours from claim notice to first documented contact from the claim contact log timestamps and derive the percent inside 24 hours.
Compare each recomputed figure to the figure published on the monthly servicing dashboard and explain any difference, since a wrong metric hides a real breach.
testing.done: all three timeliness metrics are independently recomputed, compared to the plan thresholds and reconciled to the published dashboard.

testing.step: Test every cancellation and nonrenewal against plan grounds and notice periods
actions: For each cancellation, read the ground recorded and confirm it appears in the plan-permitted grounds for that state as at the cancellation date.
Recompute the notice period actually given from the mailing date to the cancellation effective date and compare it to the longer of the plan and statutory periods.
Confirm proof of mailing exists and that the producer of record, the plan administrator and any statutory recipient were copied.
Treat a cancellation on an unpermitted ground as a reportable breach requiring flat reinstatement, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: every cancellation shows a permitted ground, a recomputed compliant notice period and proof of mailing, or a breach is raised with reinstatement.

testing.step: Re-perform the premium audit judgement on the sampled audits
actions: Open each sampled audit workpaper and independently agree the exposure basis to the source records the auditor used (payroll registers, quarterly tax filings, general ledger detail).
Re-check the classification assignment against the rating bureau scopes manual and confirm any class change carries a documented basis.
Recompute the audit premium from the verified exposure and the plan rates, and compare to the audit as billed.
For refused audits, confirm the plan noncompliance route was followed and the plan multiplier applied correctly.
testing.done: each sampled audit has an independently verified exposure, a confirmed classification and a recomputed audit premium.

testing.step: Test the insolvent-insurer block against statutory continuation and caps
actions: For each designated policy, recompute the statutory continuation end date as the earlier of policy expiration, replacement date and the statutory cut-off after the liquidation order, and compare it to the termination date applied.
For each claim paid on the block, confirm the state statutory per-claim cap and any statutory deductible were applied rather than the insolvent insurer policy limit, and recompute the payment.
Confirm the UDS submissions to the association were made on the reporting cycle and that reimbursements received reconcile to payments made.
Confirm policyholders received written notice of the estate claim-filing route before the court bar date.
testing.done: continuation dates and statutory caps are recomputed and agree, and UDS reporting and reimbursements reconcile.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying assignment number, policy number, state, exception type and the customer or pool impact.

Assign a root cause (assignment loaded outside the plan product code, voluntary rate pages used, discretionary credit applied, audit queue overflow, cancellation ground taken from the voluntary manual, late unit statistical submission) and a named owner.
For off-plan rating and improper cancellation, open the customer remediation action as well: premium refund or flat reinstatement with coverage restored from inception.
Set a remediation date and carry every open issue into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a customer remediation where one is owed, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare each recomputed metric to its plan performance standard (95% issuance, 90% audit turnaround, 95% claim contact) and compute the exception rate on rating and cancellation testing.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each supporting point and the count of policies requiring remediation.
Have the Underwriting Quality / Audit Manager, who sits outside the servicing unit and worked none of the sampled files, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any standard misses and any improper cancellations to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting, and file the workpaper under the plan and quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, metric-by-metric results and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
